original_question: Let G be a minor-closed class of graphs that excludes K_{3,t} for some positive integer t. Does there exist a threshold Delta_0 such that every graph G in this class with Delta(G) > Delta_0 satisfies both chi(G^2) <= chi_l(G^2) and chi_l(G^2) <= floor(3 Delta(G) / 2) + 1?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 9 in Section 3.1, restated in Section 6 under Open Problems and Conjectures, item 4.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper-faithful target. It has the correct hypothesis on the graph class (minor-closed and excluding K3,t for some positive integer t), the correct asymptotic threshold parameter Δ0, the correct square-coloring/list-coloring parameters, and the correct upper bound ⌊3Δ(G)/2⌋ + 1. It also mirrors the paper’s inclusion of χ(G^2) ≤ χ_ℓ(G^2), which is consistent with the notation section.
missing_details: Use different symbols for the graph class and an individual graph: the paper’s formulation is of the form 𝒢 as a class and H ∈ 𝒢 as a graph.
State that the threshold Δ0 is allowed to depend on the class 𝒢.
Replace the strict threshold Δ(H) > Δ0 with the paper’s formulation Δ(H) ≥ Δ0.
Define the square H^2 of a graph H as the graph on V(H) in which two vertices are adjacent whenever they are at distance at most 2 in H.
Define χ_ℓ(H^2) as the list chromatic number of the square.
If you want the closest paper terminology, say that such a class 𝒢 is a nice class.
For a fully stand-alone formulation, specify the ordinary finite simple graph setting assumed in the survey’s notation section.
refined_question: Let 𝒢 be a minor-closed class of finite graphs such that K3,t is not in 𝒢 for some positive integer t. Is it true that there exists an integer Δ0 = Δ0(𝒢) such that every graph H ∈ 𝒢 with maximum degree Δ(H) ≥ Δ0 satisfies χ(H^2) ≤ χ_ℓ(H^2) ≤ ⌊3Δ(H)/2⌋ + 1, where H^2 is the square of H (that is, two vertices are adjacent in H^2 exactly when their distance in H is at most 2) and χ_ℓ denotes list chromatic number?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the paper’s terminology: If 𝒢 is a nice class of graphs, then there exists Δ0 such that every graph H ∈ 𝒢 with Δ(H) ≥ Δ0 satisfies χ(H^2) ≤ χ_ℓ(H^2) ≤ ⌊3Δ(H)/2⌋ + 1.
justification: The draft is aiming at the survey’s Conjecture 9, not the planar-only conjecture. In Section 3.1 the paper defines a nice class as a minor-closed class that does not contain K3,t for some positive integer t, and then states Conjecture 9 with exactly the thresholded bound χ(H^2) ≤ χ_ℓ(H^2) ≤ ⌊3Δ(H)/2⌋ + 1 for graphs in such a class. Section 6, item 4 later restates the same conjecture in expanded form using the minor-closed/K3,t language, which is essentially the language of your draft. The notation section supplies the definitions of graph square and list chromatic number, which are the only real stand-alone items your draft leaves implicit. The paper also notes that the conjectured bound is best possible, with equality attained by the planar examples in Figure 3.
